title: Used to be good
body:
After 2 years of being a pro member, I’m now deleting this app. What started out as a helpful app for developing healthy habits has turned into an expensive to do list. Over the last two years the developers have slowly removed all features that were actually helpful like mood check-ins, habit modules. The tone has also shifted from acceptance and compassion to judging you for not finishing tasks. It’s just another thing for me to complete in the day. 

If the old features return, I would consider downloading it again, but until then I won’t recommend using this app

title: this is a helpful app but developers please remember that people in the southern hemisphere exist
body:
i’ve had it for 120 days and i think it’s a pretty good habit tracker. i have adhd which means im terrible at getting anything done and it would be unfair to blame the app for not completely curing my mental disability. but it has helped me quite a bit. i have not and will not pay for the membership but it works fine without it and doesn’t lock too many features behind the membership to the point that the app is unusable without it.  

however. it is so jarring to have summer seasonal events during midwinter. i get that statistically most people using this app are in the northern hemisphere, but i really wish there was a feature that allowed you to have seasonal events like the ‘fun in the sun’ or the cherry blossom one, during times that actually correspond to those seasons in your real life. that’s really my only complaint about it

title: The Shop System Needs a Rework
body:
I think it’s quite frustrating that the furniture and clothing shops only let you refresh once for free, and after that you’re stuck waiting or spending currency. On top of that, everything is completely random, so if you’re looking for a specific item or trying to decorate your home a certain way, you could be waiting forever.

This system feels unnecessarily restrictive. It would be much better to remove the random rotation or at least give players the option to browse and purchase the items they actually want instead of relying entirely on luck.

title: Good app- possible improvements?
body:
First of all, I love the app concept and have used for a couple months previously before stopping use. These are the ideas I have that I think would improve experience this time:
- A dark mode option for migraine/headache folks
- a option for compact tasks (having to scroll to see them can be overwhelming)
- Stacking tasks - similar to the grouping option but for breaking down tasks: for example, there’s a task called ‘put pillowcase in wash’ and when you complete it, it reveals the next task eg ‘put on new pillowcase’. Would really help as the amount of space and clutter of groups was a major factor in my stopping use, and now I’m trying again I would love to see something like this. Thanks!

title: Great concept
body: I like how it functions. I have a big issue with the “Outfits” to purchase and what can be worn, more specifically purchasing health care products like hearing aids or an insulin pump.  When choosing what my finch should wear she cannot wear her hearing aids if she chooses to wear a hat or other head gear.  Hearing aids should never be compromised for what one chooses their outfit to look like. A big part of self care is hearing and for those of us with hearing loss it would imply it doesn’t matter. There are numerous statistics linking untreated hearing loss with poor outcomes.

title: Rare un-money driven app, not too gamified, love the developers!
body: I don’t usually write reviews but it’s so rare to find such a user driven (opposed to money driven) app. I’ve been using the free version for a week, and it’s amazing. Lots of features, has really helped my routine. But the most important are the little details that show how much the developers care for each user’s wellbeing, even on the unpaid version. 1. No ad pop ups. The only way to upgrade is if you click the button. Doesn’t remind you every time you open the app. 2. Most vital sections (eg the first aid kit) are free for all users. This is amazing since it guarantees everyone the chance to use it. Shows how much they care about wellbeing. 3. No fully restricted functions. Paid users (obviously) get perks but there’s nothing unpaid users can’t get, they just get less of it. 4. Not gamified. Doesn’t try to get you addicted with additional games or time wasters. Just enough to get you interested enough in the app to actually use it. 5. There’s always something (not addicting) to do. This is great for me because I’ve found that doing an activity whenever I feel the urge to scroll really helps with my screen addiction.

title: App genuinely changed my life for the better!
body:
I decided to get Finch cause I saw one of those corny self care bed rotting apps, and honestly I was in that state and I’ve tried everything and it didn’t work so I thought why not download it.

I don’t regret it one bit. I only have the Free version right now but I really wanna invest in the paid one once I’m financially stable enough.

I suffer from ADHD and Autism and I’ve always had big goals and high achievements but I sucked in consistency and routine and keeping momentum via baby steps. I was always told routine and baby steps are literally the most important things to have because I was constantly going through periods of long burn out and unmotivated depression after a good period in my life and I just wanted the cycles to stop or at least stabilise a little bit.

Finch gave me the opportunity to finally develop consistency in my life, instead of waking up in the morning to doomscroll on TikTok I open my Finch to see how many tasks I can complete within the waking hours. I’ve been using it for almost 2 months and I’ve inadvertently created a morning routine based off Finch tasks. I never forget my meds, I never forget to shower, I used to never go gym and now I go 5-6 times a week because it’s on Finch. I’ve tried to-do lists before but they’re so boring and I end up losing or starting over or making a million of them. But the way Finch is designed as a game combined with a To-Do list actually motivates me to complete my tasks, not just ON TIME but as soon as possible. I’ve tried Habitcia and I don’t want to invalidate the app cause it’s worked for loads of other people I know, but it doesn’t feel as personal as Finch.

I also love that Finch offers a diary like system and it recommends you old tasks you’ve done.

And the best thing is it encourages you to branch out in tasks which lead me to not burning out. Before I’d hyper fixate on one aspect on my life, like skincare, fitness, study etc. which is why even when I’d achieve something great I’d burn out and not achieve anything for so long in those aspects. Finch helped me balance all the aspects of my life so I can sort my goals accordingly to them, genuinely such an amazing app. I wanted to socially isolate to focus on myself but finch reminded me I should be reaching out to my friends, I should be talking to my family. It helped me foster relationships and even be kinder to strangers.

I love this app, I’m genuinely not being paid or exaggerating, only 2 months and this app helped me develop a sense of routine and balance in all aspects of my life. I’d 100% recommend this to people with ADHD or anyone that struggles with big dreams and small steps and hyper fixation and balance. It’s so so good. Thank you Finch and thank you to the devs of this amazing app

title: A heartwarming addictive adventure app
body:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️🌟

“I’ve been playing Finch for a week now, and it has quickly become my favorite app! From the very first moment, I was drawn into this colorful, lively town full of charm and surprises. On my first day, I wandered around the town, meeting adorable characters and exploring little nooks I didn’t even know existed. I stumbled upon a tiny bakery and a beautiful park, and it felt like I had discovered a whole new world.

One of my favorite parts is collecting pets. Every day, I check on them, and they each have their own little personalities. My arctic fox loves napping by the fireplace, my tiny dragon likes to perch on shelves, and my little bunny hops around excitedly whenever I come near. It’s so rewarding to see them interact with the town and with each other—it really feels like I’m part of their world.

The quests in Finch are fun and varied. Some days I explore hidden corners of the town, other days I help characters with tasks or collect items for special events. I especially love the travel missions; they make me feel like my town is alive and full of adventures waiting to be unlocked. Each new building I unlock, from the Travel Agency to the cozy café, adds so much to the game and keeps it fresh and exciting.

I also love the social side of Finch. Visiting friends’ towns, seeing how they decorated their spaces, and interacting with their pets makes the experience even richer. The community updates are frequent and meaningful, and I can tell the developers really listen to players’ feedback. Every new update brings something fun and unexpected, so there’s always a reason to log in.

What makes Finch truly special is how it combines creativity, relaxation, and adventure. I can spend hours designing my town, checking on my pets, or exploring new areas, and it never feels repetitive. It’s a perfect escape after a long day, and it makes me genuinely happy to open the app.

I would recommend Finch to anyone who loves cute characters, interactive gameplay, and a world full of surprises. It’s one of the most engaging and heartwarming apps I’ve ever played. Every day in Finch feels like a little adventure, and I can’t wait to see what new experiences are coming next. Truly a five-star game, and I can’t imagine my day without it!”

⸻

If you want, I can also make a version that’s even longer—like a full month of adventures with your pets and favorite locations, which could really make it stand out in the App Store.

Do you want me to do that too?

title: The best mindfulness app I’ve used
body:
I have used a lot of mindfulness apps through the years, including some which have a ‘pet’ style incentive, and none have worked for me but Finch. The interface is cute and the goal setting is really easy - I especially like the guided breathing exercises and the weekly prompts to review and set new goals for the week ahead. 

The app is extremely flexible as you can change and add goals and self care areas depending on your needs. It also doesn’t make you feel bad if you miss a day, and the gentleness of this makes me feel more inspired to keep coming back to the app even if I miss a day or two. 

By using Finch, I have felt myself feeling better and I have been actually able to upkeep habits and behaviours which has been a real struggle for me. The paid version in my opinion in my opinion is really worth it if you find the app enjoyable. The check-in notifications from my buddy Chirpee also are a nice reminder through the day to look after myself and that I’m not alone as I work on my goals and happiness.

title:
A Sanctuary of Self-Care and Sophistication
★★★★★
body:
Finch is an absolute gem—a truly effortless and elegant way to weave consistent self-care into the fabric of the everyday. For those of us navigating demanding schedules, this app provides a calming anchor and a luxurious moment of respite without ever feeling like another chore. It perfectly embodies the promise of finding flow and embracing rest and recreation.
The design is refined, and the gentle nudges towards mindful reflection are exactly what is needed to maintain focus.

To elevate this experience further, I would love to suggest some exciting, sophisticated expansions for future updates that embrace the art of unspoken luxury:

1. The Traveler’s Passport: Imagine a Passport feature that tracks and showcases our Finch’s completed global adventures, complete with stylized stamps from each destination, turning discovery into a tangible keepsake.

2. The Ember & Stone Traveler’s Collection: Adding a new store collection featuring bespoke and practical travel accessories, like a miniature passport and elegant pouch for the Birb to carry, and sophisticated carry-on pieces.

3. Localized Retreat & Recreation: A "Bedroom" environment with distinct backgrounds that immediately reflect the architectural and aesthetic style of our current country—for instance, a Parisian apartment view or a Japanese ryokan—would enhance the feeling of being elegantly grounded. This could be paired with engaging virtual country-themed games to play with our Birb, such as a Japanese Zen Garden planning game or an Italian vineyard management mini-game.

4. Rewarded Social Recreation: Introducing an option to engage in elegant, multiplayer mini-games with friends and other Birbs—available exclusively after daily self-care tasks are completed—making connection a sophisticated reward for flow and focus.

5. Effortless Attire: The addition of an automatic wardrobe schedule to effortlessly transition the Birb into evening loungewear (pyjamas) and polished morning attire, aligning with our focus on flow and effortless ease.

A magnificent experience all around. Thank you for making this exquisite team gift subscription available—it’s been invaluable.

~ S. Michelle

title: I can’t believe it’s working for my ADHD - BEST APP EVER!
body:
I absolutely love this app so much. I have tried countless apps for managing my ADHD and I never stay consistent. I have almost a 100 day streak on Finch, which is UNHEARD OF for me. I love the monthly events, it makes it so much more exciting. They constantly update their Instagram with cute stuff relating to the app, including giving clues for next month’s theme and new locations for our birbs to visit. I love that I can buy clothes and furniture for my birb, I can customise its colours whenever I want, I can take it to different cities, I can add friends and do goals together, and much more. 

The 1 thing I’m really hoping to see in the future is being able to adjust how much money we earn from completing tasks. Even if we can just choose between 1-5 or 1-10, it would help me to add more value to some goals over others. 

Anyway, GET THIS APP!!!

title: TOTALLY AWESOME
body: Finch is the GREATEST and AWESOMEST and WONDERFULEST self-care app in the WORLD. It gives you a free three day preview of Finch Plus a few days after your first day. I don’t know what could be Finch Plus because Finch is already awesome and I haven’t figured out what plus means. Anyway, you get to choose the colour, name and gender of your bird and it really motivates you by letting you make your own goals and when you do them all, your Finch gets energy for………………you’ll find out when you get the app, I’m not telling you. (FOR A GREAT SURPRISE!!!) Your bird can also grow and you can watch it grow. But you do have to do Finch daily. You can also have friends on Finch and get micro pets, which are pets for your pets. Cute, right? You can also do MANY MANY MANY more new, cool things in Finch. Plus, there’s an events each month. If they can make Finch better and great and EVEN MORE AWESOME, it’s great! But I already think it’s the awesomest it can be. You can also choose what personality your bird mostly is and it develops more and more each day, when it might start TINY SUPERDUPER TINY.

title: Really enjoying this so far!
body: I have been using the Finch app for five days now, and I’m really enjoying it so far. There’s no pressure to use it, but I find myself wanting to complete the goals I’m setting for myself and opening the app in order to do so. In addition to this, the prompts to write reflections and complete breathing exercises have been great. It seems to help that I am accountable to a cute little bird, that I’m growing attached to and feel obligated to care of (while then taking care of myself). I really recommend it to those might find it hard to stick to goals and keep track of emotions, and remain focused - this can help. My only critique is that it can be a little tricky to fully grasp the icons, their significance and the content within. Maybe a central ‘home’ or ‘nest’ to access the progress etc.

title: 🌟 1-star review – Logical & Firm:
body:
I’m very disappointed with this app—not because of its features, but because of its political bias.

When selecting a region, “China” is missing, yet “Taiwan” is listed separately as if it were an independent country. This is not a small mistake—it is a clear political statement that violates the internationally recognized One-China Principle, which is supported by the United Nations and the majority of countries worldwide.

As a Chinese user, I find this deeply offensive. It shows a lack of respect for China’s sovereignty and a disregard for the feelings of millions of users. No matter how well-designed the app may be, I cannot support a product that promotes political misinformation and ignores basic facts about international law.

I urge the developers to reconsider their choices and correct this serious issue. Until then, I have uninstalled the app and will not recommend it to others

title: I love that there’s no shame
body:
I haven’t tried any other self care apps, but this one is perfect. There’s no shame when you miss a goal or don’t log in. It’s also so easy to log in, which makes it easier to keep the streak.

Also there’s so many opportunities to get Finch Plus for free, which is really nice. Not that many features are locked behind it, which is also really nice.

One of my friends that I invited to the app (mostly for the reward) ended up loving it and it’s now become a great way for me to communicate with him without having to talk or text.

I mostly just use the goals, since when I’m upset at school I don’t have my phone. But even just the goals are quite engaging. As with most things, I tend to go through phases of paying a lot of attention to Finch, but that’s why I love the lack of shame.

Also there being no ads is extremely nice, but I do kinda wish I could watch ads for more gems as there are so many things in the shops I want 😅

title: Better Than I Hoped
body: I wasn’t sure what to expect going into this… But I am pleasantly surprised to find myself enjoying this app and the rewards it grants me upon completing my IRL duties. From work to chores to basic self-care, this app gives me that instantaneous satisfaction for completing my tasks. And my little buddy grows from it. I earn stuff to give it and I feel nostalgic from back when I owned a Tamagotchi. But this one is much more customisable, personal, and rewarding for even someone like me — with diagnosed anxiety and depression, and also some undiagnosed stuff going on — and I can actually keep up with it and not feel pressured into doing anything. And the friends I can get from the Facebook page and Discord server is too many to count! And, again, nothing is pressuring me to respond! I feel… pretty safe on this app. More than I ever thought I would be. I can honestly say that I would recommend this app to anyone who struggles to do even the most basic self-care routine. I’m very surprised myself, but this is one of the ones I feel pretty okay about… borderline happy, in fact… At least give it a try. See how you like it before committing to it, like I did.

title: SO GOOD AND ACTUALLY ADHD-FRIENDLY
body: Honestly, this is the BEST self-care app I’ve ever used!! I’ve tried several habit tracking and self-care apps before, but they always felt boring, inflexible, and stress-inducing. But Finch is like a GAME CHANGER! It’s so fun, so encouraging, and genuinely useful. I’ve never felt guilt or pressure from it, which is rare. Finch offers practical tools I can easily use even when I’m unmotivated and down. It’s so straightforward and accessible. Cute but clean. I really appreciate these features on my bad days when I experience executive dysfunction because of stress and ADHD. In Finch, I never feel like I have to make an extra effort to “decide” what tools to use when I need them the most. I can tell that the team behind this knows what they’re doing. It has so many helpful features without feeling redundant at all. There are plenty of options and customisable features, but it never feels overwhelming like the other apps I’ve used, which often felt like they were designed for people with more willpower than I actually have (especially when I’m already struggling, which is why I need the app in the first place). Everything in Finch just feels right. I’ve been using Finch every day for almost a month now, and I’m still feeling positive, still genuinely willing to keep using it, and not bored. I really really love it.

author: phillip bonda

title: Life changing for ADHD, depression and anxiety
body:
A deceptively simple, thoughtful, cute and effective app that can transform mental health. Or just get you organised. It’s whatever you need it to be.

I could go on and on, but one example of the standouts that says to me “this is not a gimmick” is the First Aid and Helpline sections. 

First Aid immediately brings up targeted breathing exercises, grounding exercises, guided thought journals when you are in a depressive spiral, or a panic attack or just under a lot of stress - all designed to immediately help when you need it. Beyond that, there is a little red telephone Helpline which directs you to an external international database of helplines to quickly get you to the relevant ones for your country, on a range of topics from DV, SA and suicide prevention. This shows to me that a lot of thought has gone into this app that isn’t just cute bird outfits or fun adventures.

If you’re struggling, give this a try and I promise that you won’t regret it. 

I have a 58 day streak, and this is the first mental health app I have ever been able to maintain for more than a week. 

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
author: Reginald Worthington III

title: Cured my depression

title: A fun, joyful, easy way to access help when “The System” lets you down.
body: This app is a great tool to use! It can be a prompt for easy to achieve self care on the heavy days, a guide to steer thinking into better paths when the thoughts are darkly swirling, your own personal cheerleader during foggy days, a motivator to achieve reachable goals on the ok days, a motivator to achieve reachable goals on the good days or anything in between.  It has great tips for energy boosting that are SOOO simple, and a gentle way to start along better mobility and fitness should you wish.  It help connect you with community and helps refocus when you’re stuck.  I’ve loved the areas for journaling  -the questions have helped pinpoint many difficulties  I’ve been perplexed anout so I can have clarity and see the way forward.  And all with a cute little buddy to do it with!  I NEVER thought an app could be the platform for all this- I’m a technophobic!  I’ve only used the free part of the app, haven’t signed up for the extra features as I can’t afford it.  But after 16 days it’s helped me see that  I CAN do stuff, and things aren’t as bleak as they seem; my mood has lifted and I can get out of bed in the morning with expectancy instead of desperation and blackness.  Well done, Finch App Team!

title: Love Finch
body:
Finch is such a cute little app that actively gamifies getting things done and encourages you to make good habits. I have it with my friends and it is so fun to communicate with each other by sending each other love through Finch, and reminding ourselves to check in with each other.

One think I would LOVE to see is HealthKit integration! I use Apple Health for all of my health data, and I would love to be able to log my state of mind through Finch into Health would be fabulous. And even things like drinking water and food could all be logged using existing Finch features.

title: I want to thank the devs for improving my functioning
body: I had seen finch pop up a few times, but avoided trying it because I have tried other similar apps with no success, however this app somehow works where the others didn’t for me. As an adult person with a chronic illness and freshly diagnosed ADHD, this app has been nothing short of life changing. Its helping me change my attitude towards self care and organisation and routines, it doesn’t shame me for not completing tasks, and uses a lot of simple psychological tools which are like motivation magic. I like that I can customise what I do based on my energy needs, nothing makes me happier that getting sweet new clothes and furniture for my little bird friend, having my friends show up and go on adventures with me, and finding out what my bird learnt today. I am motivated to care for my bird in a way I am for myself.

title: Life changing self care app
body:
An adorable app that encourages self improvement and self care coupled with mental health techniques. Best habit app I have ever had and everything is free - some things are plus features but nothing that inhibit any goals or the main app :) unlike other apps. Unlike other apps, it has a lot of empathy and connects your mental
health when you’re unable to complete tasks etc :). Caring for a little finch through adventures is so fun and like a game - except also improving my life! I love this app so much and I cannot recommend it enough everyone should try it. I have some potential feedbacks - for the tasks I wish you could reorder them the day before or a lot smoother as the tasks are not in time order. I also think it requires a tutorial as I found a lot of features by accident.

author: RedCookie305_

title: Love it
body:
I don’t usually get attached to virtual pets (my history with tamagotchis will attest to this) but something about Finch is different. 

I’ve got a streak of about 89 days now of checking in on my birb and I intend on continuing. 

It’s an engaging take on self care and it works for my brain because 89 days in a row can’t lie about that. 

It gives fun insights into different areas of the world that your Finch can adventure to and explore daily too. 
The motivational messages are endearing as well and it’s safe to say I’m very attached to my virtual birb. 
The animations are simple but by goodness I wish I could hug my Finch. 

Thank you devs for somehow getting me very attached to a virtual birb. 
Your writing is endearing and the animations are adorable. 
Also, I can dress my birb up however I like which is a very cute addition to the game.

title: BEST SELF CARE APP
body:
my little sister (seven years old) told me to download this app because she wanted a friend on it. Now I (21 yrs old) use it more than her, this app has significantly helped manage my days making sure I do the usual easy tasks but also difficult tasks consistently. 
What I love about the app is that it gives you coping mechanisms like breathing exercises, yoga exercises, even just simply writing to understand yourself can really help on low days. 
I also really like that most of the content is free. There is option upgrade but it’s not necessary to use the app properly like most of the other apps.
Thank you for creating this app and please keep this app free.

title: First self-care app I’ve used more than a week!
body:
As someone with ADHD, I’ve tried many, MANY different apps in the past that gamify creating routines, but all of them have lasted about 5-10 days before I stopped using them altogether when the novelty wore off. 

I would never have tried Finch, had my best friend who swore by the app not bugged me into using 

I’m now at a 70 day streak. I wasn’t even really intending to keep using it. I’ve been trying to figure out what made this app work when so many others failed, and I think it came down to:

- the sensory-friendly, simplistic UI and interactions with your birb
- the friend feature (I can’t tell you the joy I get every day seeing my friend’s little birb join mine on an adventure 🥹)
-the extra tools that suggested really simple, achieveavle goals (like “survive the day”, or “leave the house”)
Even just the fact the app is completely useable free, with the premium-only features mainly limited to cosmetic things like guaranteed outfits and extra slots in the shop.  

Whatever the case, the app has done wonders for motivating me every day, and helping me feel accomplished completing the little things on days where that was really, really hard.

In short, thank you to the devs for this wonderful lil’ app!! 

(P.S I’d love to see New Zealand or Australia added as a travel destination 👀🇦🇺🦘)

title: Great app - small improvements would be good
body:
I was hesitant to try this app because I saw it had paid features and was worried anything helpful would be trapped behind a paywall but I was pleasantly surprised to see it wasn’t that way, the paid features only unlock a kind of battle pass with more and special rewards but it’s not anything crazy and there’s still a free battle pass too, the only other thing I noticed was the paid version had more activities you could choose to do or log in but you can also just put in your own custom ones so it really doesn’t matter. I do this this app is beneficial for neurodivergent people I have autism and adhd and have found it has helped especially when you can link the progress of some things to a certain task like brushing teeth is linked to a pet being hatched which makes me really wanna do it 

The only 2 reasons I’m not rating this 5 stars is;

1, after about 3 tasks completed your lil guy will go on an adventure and at that point you will receive only half the amount of gems until the next day: like before he leaves a task will give you 5 energy, but once he leaves the same task will give you 2-3 gems, and this makes me not want to complete tasks, although it’s nice to get gems it feels like a punishment that it’s less and it makes me unmotivated to do tasks once he’s gone on an adventure, which is a shame because usually by my morning routine he’s gone so I find it hard to care for my night time tasks and wish there was more incentive.  The ingame items are so expensive I think they could just give us the same amount of gems as the energy we would have gotten if he was still at home and I think that’d be enough to incentivise tbh cos it just feels crappy knowing you did a task that’s really hard for you to only get a tiny reward for it that really does nothing, like you’d have to do hundreds of those tasks to be able to buy anything, 

2, and I feel bad about this one 😅 but the finch is really ugly, I find myself put off by it’s strange design and it feels like no matter what clothing I put on them they just always look bad and it never looks right or matches, the shop keep finches look fine I think cos they have hair but you have a wierd bald guy and it just makes me not care about him I wish they’d chosen a cuter animal or design, it just feels like everything looks wrong on them and that makes me not care to save up for clothes cos they just never look good, I also wish you could change your finches colour cos you’re locked in from your first choice when you start the game and I feel like I chose an extra ugly one 😭 I feel bad but I just don’t think he’s a cute mascot and it puts me off a bit 😭 I wish they chose a cuter animal or you could choose between different animals or something , cos currently I just find myself not attached to him at all and it makes me not care for his adventures or growth when I wish I did, and I feel bad but it also makes the app less appealing to me
author: Kakakakkakakakakkama

title: Take a chance on Finch
body:
I got mental illness, so self care and healthy habits are hard for me to stick to. Especially when I can't think of a reason "why" I should do them. My memory is also pretty bad so sometimes I just forget to do those healthy things altogether. Finch has changed that for me. 

I've used it every day for the past 3 weeks and it's helped me remember to take meds, it's motivation to do the self care that can be so hard at times. It's even helped me with mindfulness and breathing! And that's always been a struggle. 

I adore the reflections it prompts, and the first aid kit is actually filled with skills I've learnt in therapy. Being in "crisis mode" can make it hard to access those skills, so having them compiled in the app makes it so much easier to lower the distress. 

I never write reviews for apps but this little one has seriously changed my life for the better. Thanks Finch team ❤️

title: ADHD and motivated to do things??
body:
I have struggled with daily goals, habit trackers and to-do lists for so long, they just don’t seem to work for me, but this app is actually making me excited and motivated to do things. I have only been using it for a few days - usually I download these kinds of apps, and then immediately delete them because they don’t suit my needs or they require a payment immediately and I’m not willing to pay before I know I will use the app. I’m currently on the free trial and, VERY unusually for me, now 100% committed to paying for the 1 year subscription at the end of my 7 days. I really think it’s very reasonably priced (AUD$60 / year). I have replaced doom scrolling with hanging out on this app, chatting to my bird (Birdy), decorating her house, and organising my goals and habits. Every morning I make my bed and vacuum my bedroom straight away because I want to hatch my egg. I don’t care how childish this is (I’m 28), it’s literally making me feel positive about life again. I am embracing who I am as a person (5 yr old in a 28 yr olds body, love little baby animated birds, can’t wait to save up and buy my bird a new wallpaper). The affirmations and messages feel so genuine and positive, I really feel seen and uplifted every time I read them or get a notification or open the app. 

My favourite thing about the app is it really feels like a rare example of something that is truly designed to make people’s lives better. The UI and design is amazing, beautiful, adorable and consistent, and the only way you can progress in the game and get little fun digital things is by doing your actual real life tasks, goals and self care habits. It’s fricking amazing. And the AI features are really impressive too, like the week summaries and insights and stuff. I haven’t really explored it properly yet but I get the feeling there’s some impressive (and helpful) analysis going on behind the scenes. Anyway, sorry for the long review and thank you so much developers for making this app. 

FEATURE REQUEST: wallpapers - I want my whole phone to be in the finch universe, and I love all the animations and art so much. I’d love to be able to go full-screen mode or something in the forest or in my finch’s house and take a screenshot or download a wallpaper to use as a screen saver on my phone :)
author: ilovetwelve

title: Great Additional Tool
body:
When it comes to ADHD and Autism, for me, they often win the day - meaning I don’t achieve nearly as much as I like, and I’ve tried dozens of techniques and apps to help me out.

Finch had been popping up on my timelines for a while before I finally clicked to see what it was all about.

Here’s what I love: easily accessible to-do lists. Tasks are easy to add and to reassign to different days. The reflective exercises are great. Don’t just skip these - they’re great slow down and think moments. Are we reflecting on stuff we deep down already know? Sure, but the reminders are great when everything gets lost in the noise of every day life.

What don’t I love? Well … I’d love if I could see a calendar of assigned tasks. I know that, even for me, that might lead to overwhelm, but some users may enjoy having that forward looking tool. Having said that, I’m nowhere near an expert on this app, so perhaps someone can tell me where that feature already exists?

One sentence review: great to slow down the mind, pause for thought, and go easier on ourselves. Oh, and I’m much more productive, too. 

Thanks, Finch.

title: I love it, but…
body:
I have a pretty complex mental health history. I’m slaying the game most days, and finch has been a massive part in me achieving a level of wellness I once dreamed of. 

Sometimes I just can’t get out of bed or achieve much though. 

I open my finch app and look at everything I was doing the week before and I feel like it’s set on hard mode, and right now I need to live on easy mode. 

I wish instead of having to remove all my goals and put in new ones such as ‘survive the day’ ‘brush teeth’ ‘eat a meal’, I could just select one of two or three lists that I know I can accomplish for the day. 

I get so depressed deleting the goals that I’ve worked so hard to get to when I’ve hit a rough spot and starting all over again. 

Easy, medium or hard mode for the day is sort of how I think about the way I function. 

Maybe something like that would help people with executive function , chronic health conditions and complex mental health struggles.

title: Life Changer
body:
I’ve struggled with executive dysfunction for my whole life. I always get told to use timers and planners and diaries and they never work. My brain doesn’t understand delayed gratification and so I just don’t do the thing I need to do even if it’ll logically take five seconds.

Finch gives me that immediate reward my brain seeks and motivates me to keep it up. It’s great for my ADHD, it’s very helpful for my depression, and although it’s by no means cured any of my problems it makes things feel a little easier. If I get stuck in bed doomscrolling in the mornings making myself late, I pull up Finch and in order to say that i have completed the task “get out of bed” I have to stand up, breaking the doomscrolling cycle. It’s great. I highly recommend for my fellow ADHDers. 

I’m also extremely emotionally attached to my baby bird and if I can’t afford to travel the world at least she gets to :)

title: Easy neurodivergent friendly routines
body: I’ve used this app for nearly a year now and it works amazingly. I’m auDHD (autistic and adhd) and was looking for an app that helped me built routine for ages and I think I found it with finch. Most apps focus on streaks and having to use the app everyday but I’ve always found that over whealming and stressful. Finch is there whenever I need it, and nothing more. I use it to keep track and remind me to wash my face and brush my teeth at night but if I don’t do those things it doesn’t punish me. I also love the breathing exercises on here, they are timed and you can pick different times and types of breathing. It’s nice and visual so I can just sit there and focus on my breathing for a minute then go about my day I love reflecting on my day with finch because I don’t have to get up and get a book and pen. I can do it thought the day witch I really like. Also my bird rocky has a mushroom hat and an autism pride flag, what more could you want .

title: best app i’ve ever downloaded

This app is the only thing that has worked for me after trying countless other apps and techniques, as it allows me to keep track of my goals and tasks whilst showing physical progress in my birb. On days when i can’t get out of bed, i somehow make it out with the thought of making Bagel (my birb) happy. Thanks so much to the devs, you’ve changed my perspective on life for the better, and i would highly recommend this app to anyone (especially neurodivergent people)

title: Finch is changing and saving lives
body:
Finch has led to huge improvements in my health.  The developers really ‘get’ how hard it can be to stay alive and keep functioning. 

When I first started using Finch, at suggestion of a psychologist who had heard about it, it felt manageable. The simple starting goals - ‘survive the day’, ‘get out of bed’ - were ones I related to. 

I couldn’t achieve much, but I did manage to survive the day. 

‘Finally, something that’s achievable for me’, I thought.

I haven’t bothered to make my bed for many years - ‘what’s the point? What difference will that make’. But it does make a difference. 

I’ve now been able to add more goals and am functioning better than I have in many years.

When I look at what’s changed since I started using Finch that could otherwise explain why I’m doing better, there’s one thing, but I truly think it’s mainly Finch.

It’s amazing how being kind to an artificial bird on a screen can lead to greater self care and improved functioning.

I really like how the data only stays on your phone, so there’s no corporate spying or data theft. With so much surveillance, lack of privacy, hacking etc these days, that’s an important feature. 

Thank you to the developers for your wonderful initiative. You are changing - and saving - many lives.

And it's not a cheap scam for developers to force people to buy 'premium'. There are no ads and the apps is perfectly useable without any money spent! 

Also you actually want to keep the goals to keep your little birdie happy!! ❤️

The interface is so easy to use and I would highly recommend to anyone!

Thanks 🫶🫶

title: Amazing app!
body:
Finch is truly an amazing app and is such an incredible self care app, and very easy to use!

To anyone who is thinking about downloading Finch, DOWNLOAD IT!! In this app you can set your own goals, and once you’ve completed them, your finch gains energy. You look after your little finch, as well as a micro pet. Once your finch grows up, you are able to unlock a new feature! They also have seasonal events which is your chance to earn gems, outfits, and, even a cute little micro pet! 🐣

Now I have been sponsored by a guardian  🌈       ( which is someone who has the membership) and I am forever grateful for it, and for anyone wondering if there’s no point if you don’t have the membership, that’s not true, the only thing that’s different is that you unlock different things .

Thank you for your time 

Finch is a must have for your device/s

- from a fellow Finch user ❤️🐥🩷

title: Genuinely the best
body:
I’ve been using Finch for over a year now and I can genuinely say my little bird has gotten me through a lot. Taking care of yourself to take care of a little birb baby works so so well, I love seeing her go on adventures and learn new things and grow, I love buying her new clothes and furniture, it gives me a reason to make my bed and brush my teeth on days when I just want to hide away. 

When my grandpa passed away I struggled a lot and it only took a couple of days before the app recommended me grief exercises/prompts everyday. It was really strangely comforting to have some recognition that every single day was hard and full of grief when so many people just moved on and expected me to as well. It really helped me process things a lot better too. 

Couldn’t be more thankful to the team who made this app, you guys have made such a huge difference to my life.

title: An interactive diary
body:
I found this app just under a week ago. After beginning to be in a bad place again. Negative feelings and bad habits arising again are something I’m trying to avoid in order to grow as a person.
I had a look at the reviews and felt hopeful from what everyone was saying.
Well, they weren’t lying. This is an excellent idea that ACTUALLY focuses on the goals at hand (thinking positively, increasing focus etc. whatever yours may be).
It prompts you to reflect, but it’s something you can choose to do. You can receive rewards for completing your goals even if you had a bad day. Through that bad day there are breathing exercises and prompts to identify why this happened and what we CAN control.
This app has allowed me to look further into what I’m feeling, why I’m feeling this way and where I can take steps to feel better.
Identifying why you may feel sad or anxious etc. instead of just feeling it has helped incredibly.

The most encouraging part is that you’re helping your character grow by helping yourself! 

I will be recommending this to the people I know will need it and can’t thank you enough for the idea.
 
They do ask a lot if you’d like to upgrade to the paying service, but this is as any system would. And you don’t miss out by saying no! Truly something that caters to everyone and focuses on the most important person here; you!

The app combines previous popular methods of staying on track in life including diary reflections and todo lists with the act of taking care and strengthening your bond with your pet. title: GREAT APP FOR MENTAL HEALTH SUPPORT <3
body:
It has so many great features that allow you to clear your head and reflect on how you’re feeling throughout the day! 
You can set daily or weekly goals to complete,
There are breathing and movement exercises, There are soundscapes you can play for relaxing, There are a few quizzes you can do, 
There’s a ‘first aid’ section if you’re experiencing anxiety to help you ground and ease the anxiety, 
There’s a ‘deep dive’ section where you can set your triggers and what helps when you’re experiencing any of those that you can access when you need,
It follows your moods and reflections and gives you an overall chart of your day and week and the pros and cons of that week,
For fun, you have a Finch you can name, choose pro-nouns, accessorise and buy clothes for (you get ‘energy’ to spend whenever doing things on the app. You’ll get ‘energy’ from writing in your diary etc). And decorate their house.
Every day your Finch will ask a random life question, you have two choices to choose between as they grow and develop their personality which is fun. I kinda wish they asked more though!

title: LOVE this app!
body:
I have ptsd, anxiety, depression + more. This app has been an absolute lifesaver for keeping my anxiety under control, improve my self esteem (including stop relying on others for self esteem!) helping me use gratitude and positive psychology combined with CBT techniques to feel more optimistic in the world and myself. This also provides a safe and positive environment in which to heal and have a list of things you need to get done. 
My boyfriend got it too and we love sending each other good vibes! It’s really improved my outlook on life and given me a safe space in which to rant, calm myself, appreciate the world around me etc. Also raising a little bird makes you feel important and that you need to help it explore the world! 
I’d recommend this app to absolutely anyone for any purpose and I can’t promote it enough. Thank you Finch developers!!

title: Amazing, Thank You Finch Team!
body:
Hi Finch Team <3 I’m really really thankful for this amazing app. Nino and Steph are amazing, and have created a wonderful app. And the rest of the Finch Team are fantastic too!!! 
Finch has helped a lot with my mental health, and has helped me become a better person. There’s so many features, and so many wonderful things to help everyone! Some people may say that it’s bad because you have to pay money, but I don’t think so! You guys need to make money, and some people just don’t understand that. Keep on doing what you’re doing! I also love the customisation, it really makes the app your own. My bird is Waffles, and I love them! <3 I also love the tree town and the fact that members of the Finch Team can visit you. 
If I could suggest a few things: 
I think it would be so cool to be able to design your own clothes, and maybe more bird customisations. 
Having a full house with proper rooms and different rooms to unlock would be great as well! 
Adding some relaxing colourings or character design/house design sort of areas would be very de-stressing, and I know I’d love something like that. (For a bit more depth, it would be nice to have something like those design games as like a relax section or something, then have colourings). 
Also, I’d like to have a yearly goal thing, so you can set goals for next year. Or monthly, weekly, or even just an eventual goal. 
Other than that, Finch is SO good! This app is just wonderful and perfect and AMAZING!!! Keep doing what you’re doing, never give up, know that this app has helped me and so many others, and know that you are AWESOME! 
Edit: I also would love to have a happy lift-up section, with motivational quotes, and things sort of saying, you’re awesome! And stuff. Not quotes like when you open the app, but things to help if you’re feeling down. And they could look like they’re being said by the Finch Team or people in your tree town. 
Melody :D

title: Great for personal growth and goals
body:
Okay, I know this app is designed for self-care, which it does exceptionally well, but I generally feel pretty good already, so I got creative to find ways of keeping the cute little finchie in my life:

How to Use Finch as a Goal Planner:
- Go to ‘Journey’ section (top right hand icon) 
- Choose from existing options, or
- Add your own (for me, this is where the magic happens)

You can do all this for free, by the way.

I use a paper goal planner which is great for big picture (quarterly, monthly) planning, but I’m pretty useless at keeping track of daily and weekly habits. So I input them into this app and finchie reminds me. Once a habit becomes second nature, I delete it and add new ones.

Could I use another app for this purpose? Sure, but I haven’t come across another one that has that Duolingo-esque aesthetic and rewards system. And I like to imagine that as finchie is adventuring and growing, so am I. 

I also like the reminder to invest in all areas of life, like friendships, trying new things and caring for others.

If you’re here for the self-care resources, there’s a mind-boggling variety:
- Breathing exercises
- Relaxation stretches 
- Guided reflection prompts 
- Sleep hygiene techniques 
- Quizzes to gauge mental health status 
- Mental health first aid strategies 
- Soundscapes 
- Community building capacity 
And lots more. A lot of it is free. I personally think that just the sight of little finchie is enough to give everyone a boost :)

title: It’s my best friend
body:
As so many people in the reviews have said, it’s a miracle how long I want to stick with this app. Having someone there who is excited to see you, who you’re able to encourage and interact with, does wonders for accountability. I love the supportive messages that Finch sends throughout the day. I’ve also really appreciated the thoughtful prompts and goal-setting mechanisms. 

I’ve always enjoyed journaling and find writing out my feelings to be cathartic, but when I’m at my lowest, even that can feel pointless. Writing to Finch, knowing that it will benefit the character and giving me the feeling that someone cares and listens, really motivates me to get my thoughts down and bring myself back up. I’ve struggled with ups and downs in depression and it says a lot that I want to keep coming back to this app even at my worst. 

I’ve been using Finch for months now - maybe close to a year - and I’m still loving it. Thank you!

title: A journal that listens and talks back
body:
My wife recommended this app to me a few weeks ago as I have trouble expressing my feelings and get too caught up in my own head. 

As of this review I have written over 2.4k words and already feel a difference with my day to day mood swings. 

The one day that I ignored writing in Finch I noticed that I was more irritable and quick to frustration when dealing with inconvenient life situations. When used regularly though I have noticed that I can either calm or move through my emotions smoothly.

As said in the title, this is a journal, but it feels like one that literally talks back to you. Your finch companion regularly sends positive comments whenever a push notification comes through from the app, and the writing prompts are really useful when you don’t know where to start. You can also add other users and send them motivation through an easy tap of a button.

What I like most though is that the app monitors what you are writing, attaching hashtags to key words. It then compiles this information, giving regular summaries of what you have been feeling positive about and what you have been feeling negative about. This is where the app really shines.

I recommend using Finch if you have trouble sifting through your emotions and get too caught up in your own self talk. The first steps to mindfulness lie within, good luck!

TLDR - This app is a journal that talks back to you and you will find with regular use that your equilibrium of emotions will balance out.

title: Fantastic
body:
My depression has dropped from severe to moderate and this app has helped with that. Recommendations for developers:
1. Once you’ve gone on adventures it looks like there’s not much to do but I like that the extra energy goes towards gems at least.
2. More interactions with the finch would be cute, I had to google how to pet the finch I don’t remember that being shown, it says it wants to chat but I don’t think it’s an option unless it’s end of an adventure?
3. I like that you can adjust the bedtime so that finch is awake when you might check on it, it would be even better if you could select if a goal goes towards that days or the day before. For example I’ve checked off my ‘drink water’ goal whilst I was still up at 1am and this results in me not being promoted to complete that goal for that next day as it’s already checked off.

Thank you for this app!!

title: Best self care app I’ve ever tried
body:
I’ve tried a bunch of different meditation/journalling/self care apps over the last few years and this is absolutely the best one for me. While there is a paid subscription option, it’s much cheaper than most other apps that do similar things, and you can still get a lot out of the app without needing to pay anything or sign up for a free trial. 
I also like that the default settings have  information stored on your phone rather than external drives/the cloud/wherever. 
Finch also just has so many different options and is really good at letting you choose what parts to use- for example it gives you prompts for writing reflections, goals, grounding exercises etc but you don’t have to use the suggested prompts. I also just really like the finch pet and it’s reflections on its experiences are genuinely just really sweet and uplifting. Overall a really good app!

title: Great for neurodiverse adults too!!
body:
A bunch of my friends (we're all neurodivergent in some form, and all 21+) have difficulty maintaining daily habits and getting even small stuff done without motivation. We've all found since using Finch that our general motivation is higher!! It has so many useful features and even the free version has so much it's super usable even without the paid content, which just seems like some extensions on the already wide capabilities it offers. It's cute, you can add your friends in order to help them out and send cute little acts of kindness, it has some really handy tools like soundscapes, stretching and breathing exercises, and depression/anxiety tracking, and it's super intuitive to use, so even though I've only been using it a few days, I can see myself using it far into the future!! The ability to block certain tags is super handy to keep triggering suggestions out also, it's not something you see often, and it's not super demanding and annoying like a lot of habit tracking apps <3

TLDR: great, easy app, with heaps of free content and really hard working devs. Stuff is constantly in the works and it's all useful features! Sensitive to topics other tracking apps aren't, and really handy with general mental health tools.

title: Finch disliking things ruins the experience 😔
body:
My partner and I downloaded this app a few weeks ago and we’ve really enjoyed doing the reflection exercises and sending each other cute “See who’s visiting” check-ins throughout the day.

However we’ve noticed that even when we click the same response for something that Finch found during their adventures, I will always get “(Finch) dislikes XY” but my partner will always get “(Finch) likes XY“. This has happened five times now.

I am a naturally pessimistic person so I use mindfulness apps like these to bring happiness and positivity into my day, and it really upsets me when my Finch seems to dislike everything as well. It’s gotten to the point where I don’t even want to make her go on adventures anymore for fear of her disliking more things.

Please remove or at least lessen the amount of dislikes! I would have easily given 5 stars if not for this feature, and now I am seriously considering abandoning this app.

title: This app tricks you into looking after yourself.

title: Great app, some very minor issues
body:
I’ve been using the app for about a month now and the daily goals feature has been really helpful for me. I’ve had very minimal issues with the app, up until today. 

Previously I was able to write my own goals no problem, but whenever I try to write a goal that is more than 1 word, it deletes all but the first word. When I try to edit it nothing changes, and when I try to delete them from my goals altogether they just keep coming back and, more of them?

There is also some features I would like to see changed/added, for example-
1) If I make a typo in a goal or reflection, the app seems to think it’s an actual word and will register it as one of the purple things/objects(?), and I can’t delete them?
2) I somewhat understand the thought behind it, but it’s frustrating that quite a few of the features are Finch Plus only. Like editing icons for the purple things/objects, or some of the breathing exercises.
3) I’m unsure if this is already a feature and I’ve just not found it, but I would really like to see more colour options for the pet(?), and a setting to be able to edit it later on.
4) It would also be nice to be able to pick from every clothing option when buying, not just what’s in the store that day.
5) Sometimes, if you’ve used/added them enough, personal goals you add will stick and go into the recommended goals for the day, and that is great- I would just find it more useful if I could add personal goals to a section where I can always find and use them, rather than typing them out every day until the app picks up on it.

TLDR; The app is really helpful and I’ve gotten a lot of happiness and motivation out of it in the short amount of time I’ve been using it. I have some small nitpicks, but they’re nothing too important, so I can see past them. If it weren’t for the issues I mentioned I would for sure give 5 stars, this is the only self care app I’ve stuck with for so long and can see myself continuing to use in the future. 😊

title: Best self-care app out
body: Love the app and love that it’s by just two people! Saw the reviews and couldn’t believe what magic you’ve created! You clearly understand the biggest issue with CBT/self-care apps is that it’s HARD to be accountable for your own self-care. I would use other self-help apps ONLY on days I felt good and could never motivate myself to actually face them on bad days. What your app offers is the encouragement that self-care will grow SOMETHING more than just your mental well-being. You are attaching a physical concept to self-care and checking in and making it so so so much easier to do for a lot of people. You advertised to me on a day I had a complete relapse and I downloaded it on the spot. I have used it every day since and I am shocked that it’s been a week and I’m still checking in daily - and now enjoying it! Thank you for realising the problem consumers face and answering it. title: Amazing! Something special that meshes well with my neurodivergent brain
body:
I was reading through other reviews before writing mine and saw that there’s just two of you working on Finch! I was so surprised because this app is better than any other I’ve used in the realm of self care/journaling.

I’ve been using Finch for just over a week and it’s helped me with multiple panic attacks and overall feeling better. I have chronic severe anxiety and depression as well as ADHD and ASD so there’s a lot going on in my brain. My mum actually commented that an app like this is good for people like me who struggle to engage in therapy and need a resource accessible all the time.

Since I’m mentioning my mum, I’ll point out that I’m an adult, I just still live in the family home. That shouldn’t matter but people reading reviews may think I’m a ten year old who got ahold of their parents’ iTunes password and take this review less seriously so I decided to clarify. 

Artichoke (the name of my buddy) is adorable and the daily adventures aren’t only a motivator for me to check in on myself throughout the day but also they’re helping me view things from a new perspective thanks to their childlike wonder. 

Speaking of ‘their’, I appreciate the pronoun options in Finch so much! I’m nonbinary so it’s so cool to be able to have a buddy who uses the same pronouns as me. It would be cool to have more pronoun options at some point in the settings for people who use neos and stuff! Just a thought, not an expectation.

Anyway, I’m loving the new update/layout and can’t wait for Finch to become more widely known since it’s genuinely so good and fills a whole in the ‘market’ for people like me <3

title: First app I’ve used for longer than 3 days for habits & self care
body:
Honestly, I’ve never opened most habit, self care, daily journal apps more than once.
I’m on Day 3 of 7 trialling premium, and honestly it’s an amazing app. I believe some slight feature additions would be great which I’ll list below:
- An easier way to access and review goals you set for future dates (like a calendar, maybe 2-3 days though), such as “set goals for tomorrow”,
- A reminder if something is already on your goals list for that day, and an option to add it any way (ie brushing teeth)
- Restyling of some of the questions in auto tagged text submissions when clicked on in the “Add to goals” section as some don’t make sense, ie, I’ve had “Schedule time for soap” with #Soap
- Some extra categories for things like Hygiene, or the ability to write something in the “Other” options

I think you’ve got really great, solid foundations to build on.
Really great job, I think it’s going to become very popular.
